title: D1-1b-HS: Candidate Membrane Screening under High-Salinity Variability
question_prompt:
D1-1b-HS: Candidate Membrane Screening under High-Salinity Variability

An SWRO intake experiences substantial salinity variability while membrane area and design pressure are fixed. Procurement offers four membrane candidates. Screen them at a high-salinity nominal condition, stress only the passing shortlist at an even higher salinity, prune failed branches, and verify the survivor(s) at low and high temperature before selection.

Fixed parameters | Value | Unit | Notes | Design / stress case | NaCl mass fraction | Temperature °C | Feed pressure bar
Feed mass flow | 4.073 | kg/s | Fixed | Nominal | 0.033 | 30 | 56
Membrane area | 390 | m² | Fixed | High salinity stress | 0.036 | 30 | 56
Nominal feed pressure | 56 | bar | Fixed | Low temperature verify | 0.033 | 22 | 56
Permeate pressure | 1.013 | bar | Fixed | High temperature verify | 0.033 | 36 | 56
Pressure drop | 0.653 | bar | Fixed
Channel height | 0.002 | m | Fixed | Common hard constraints (all mandatory cases)
Spacer porosity | 0.75 | - | Fixed | Qp | ≥ 5.70 m³/h
Module length | 20 | m | Fixed | Recovery | ≤ 48.0%
Flux | ≤ 17.5 LMH
Four candidate membranes (new parameter set; not the fixed M1–M4 set) | Rejection | ≥ 99.10%
Membrane | A_comp | B_comp | Design intent | Permeate NaCl | ≤ 300 mg/L
HS-X Productivity | 5.1e-12 | 4.6e-08 | High A / high B
HS-Y Throughput-balanced | 4.7e-12 | 3.4e-08 | High A / medium B
HS-Z Salt-robust balanced | 4.3e-12 | 2.2e-08 | Balanced A / low B
HS-W Ultra-rejection | 3.8e-12 | 1.5e-08 | Lower A / ultra-low B

1. E1 — Identify this as a membrane-performance parameter selection problem. Explain the A/B trade-off and the likely failure modes of high-A/high-B and low-A/low-B candidates.
2. E2 — Screen all four candidates fairly at the nominal condition. Only membranes satisfying every hard constraint may enter the shortlist.
3. E3 — Run the high-salinity stress only on the shortlist. Eliminate failed candidates immediately and stop those branches.
4. E4 — Verify the final stress-test survivor(s) at 22/36°C low/high temperature. Recommend only after all mandatory cases pass.
5. Final recommendation — Use the margins in production, flux, recovery, rejection and permeate NaCl; do not rank membranes only by highest A or lowest B.

Task version: D1-1b-HS; difficulty calibrated to the prior hard D1-1b tasks; candidate parameters and the gold path were verified with ROprocess.simulate_ro.
reference_answer:
D1-1b-HS：Gold Answer — Screening → Shortlist → Stress Test

Reference efficient trajectory: about 8 simulate_ro calls: 4 nominal-screening calls → 2 shortlist stress calls → 2 final temperature-verification calls. The correct final candidate is HS-Z. Equivalent adaptive orders are acceptable if pruning and mandatory evidence are complete.
